text:
Elaine: Customer opened a support case: tool_call in streaming mode throws JSON parse errors intermittently.
Marco: can you drop the request_id and any connection id?
Elaine: req=01H9ZXA2 conn=conn-2b3c. Customer attached their raw SSE capture.
Elaine: Customer capture (literal SSE lines):

```
data: {\"type\":\"tool_call\",\"tool\":\"lookup-faq\",\"args\":\"{\"q\":\"billing\",\"cursor\":0,\"notes\":\"long...\"...\"}\n\

data: {\"id\":\"01H9ZXA2\",\"args_cont\":\"more text that finishes the JSON\"}
```

Priya: it looks like the JSON object inside the data: field is being split across multiple SSE events. The client treats each data chunk as a complete JSON blob and fails on partial payloads.
Tom: are they using our JS client or rolling their own?
Elaine: they used a bare node-fetch stream parser. They say our official SDK buffers and avoids the issue.
Marco: we shipped a minor change last week that flushes the SSE buffer sooner to reduce tail latency. That can create split writes if origin performs multiple write() calls for one logical event.
Priya: edge logs (Fastly) show two write segments for the same event at 2029-02-11T15:12:03Z; no retransmits or connection resets.
Elaine: customer error message: \"Unexpected end of JSON input\" from JSON.parse when handling event.data.
Marco: short repro plan: run a local SSE server that writes a 3KB args payload in two write() calls and observe node-fetch behavior. I can repro locally.
Elaine: customer shared minimal repro steps:
1) POST /v1/stream with tool_call payload
2) Server emits single SSE event but sends payload in multiple TCP writes
3) Client's per-event parsing runs JSON.parse on each data chunk -> throws on partial chunk

Elaine: example bytes they captured (simplified):
```
<data chunk A>
{\"type\":\"tool_output\",\"tool\":\"lookup-faq\",\"args\":{\"q\":\"billing\",\"limit\":100,\"notes\":\"very long text starts here...\"\n
</data chunk A>
<data chunk B>
...rest of notes...\"}}
</data chunk B>
```

Marco: immediate mitigation options:
- revert the aggressive SSE flush so we only flush when the full event payload is ready, or
- add explicit per-event framing (e.g., a Content-Length equivalent inside the SSE payload) so clients can assemble parts, or
- document client-side defensive parsing (buffer until braces balance).

Priya: logs indicate the origin app did two separate write() calls without inserting the required SSE event delimiter (double newline). We should enforce that origin writers include the event terminator.
Marco: pushing a canary that buffers SSE writes until the event body is complete. Will monitor latency impact.
Elaine: I told the customer the SDK avoids the issue and offered the brace-balance buffer workaround. They prefer a server-side fix.
Marco: created INF-3310 in our tracker for the runtime fix and asked eng-runtime to watch the canary.
ops-bot: ticket INF-3310 created by Marco. Priority: P2. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-3310
Elaine: I'll send the customer an interim note with repro guidance and recommended client buffering pattern.
Marco: long-term: add explicit per-event framing header or guarantee we never emit partial JSON inside a single SSE event.
Elaine: filing follow-up doc with examples for Node/Go clients showing robust SSE parsing patterns. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
